title: ERC-7710: Smart Contract Delegation
quote: This proposal introduces a standard way for smart contracts to delegate capabilities to other smart contracts or Externally Owned Accounts (EOAs). The delegating contract (delegator) must be able to authorize a `DelegationManager` contract to call the delegator to execute the desired action. ... A Delegator is a smart contract that can create a delegation. A Delegation Manager is a smart contract that validates delegation authority and calls on the Delegator to execute an action. A delegate is a smart contract, smart contract account, or EOA that has authority to redeem a delegation. ... When a delegate wishes to redeem a delegation, they call the `redeemDelegations` function on the Delegation Manager and pass in the action they want to execute and the proof of authority (ie delegation). ... Additionally, this proposal is compatible with ERC-4337, although its implementation does not necessitate ERC-4337. Requires EIP-1271, EIP-7579.

title: ERC-7715: Request Permissions from Wallets
quote: We define a new JSON-RPC method `wallet_requestExecutionPermissions` for DApp to request a Wallet to grant permissions in order to execute transactions on the user's behalf. ... The permission response data will be redeemable by the `account` defined in the `to` field, using the interfaces specified in ERC-7710 ... calls its `redeemDelegation` function using the `_permissionContexts` parameter set to the returned `permissions.context`.

title: MetaMask Delegation Framework (DeleGator Smart Accounts)
quote: A DeleGator Smart Account is a 4337-compatible Smart Account that implements delegation functionality. ... A Delegation enables the ability to share the capability to invoke some onchain action entirely offchain in a secure manner. ... The Delegation Manager includes the logic for validating and executing Delegations. ... Caveats are used to add restrictions and rules for Delegations ... They are managed by Caveat Enforcer contracts.

title: DelegationManager — MetaMask Delegation Framework
quote: function redeemDelegations(bytes[] calldata _permissionContexts, ModeCode[] _modes, bytes[] calldata _executionCallDatas) external; ... Ensures each delegation has sufficient authority to execute, given by the previous delegation or by being a root delegation. ... Delegations are ordered from leaf to root. The last delegation in the array must have the root authority.

title: Caveats reference — MetaMask developer documentation
quote: The Delegation Toolkit provides out-of-the-box caveat enforcers for common restriction patterns. ... The valueLte caveat enforcer uses the ValueLteEnforcer.sol contract and accepts a value as a bigint, e.g. caveatBuilder.addCaveat("valueLte", 1_000_000_000_000_000_000n). The allowedTargets caveat enforcer uses the AllowedTargetsEnforcer.sol contract and takes a list of target addresses.

title: Delegation — MetaMask developer documentation
quote: Redelegation is a core feature that sets delegations apart from other permission sharing frameworks. It allows a delegate to create a delegation chain, passing on the same or reduced level of authority from the root delegator. ... if Alice grants Bob permission to spend 10 USDC on her behalf, Bob can further grant Carol permission to spend up to 5 USDC on Alice's behalf. ... In a delegation, the authority field contains either the hash of the parent delegation, or the constant ROOT_AUTHORITY.

title: What is the Delegation Toolkit and what can you build with it?
quote: Let AI agents trade on your behalf by assigning limited execution permissions via ERC-7710, with ERC-7715 making it easy to approve those permissions through your wallet. An agent can be granted permission to spend 10 USDC per day to buy ETH, without requiring per-transaction approval.

title: x402 Documentation — Overview
quote: If payment is required, the server responds with `402 Payment Required`, including payment instructions. The buyer prepares and submits a payment payload. The server verifies and settles the payment independently, or by leveraging an x402 facilitator's /verify and /settle endpoints. ... Native support for machine-to-machine payments, enabling seamless use by AI agents.

title: x402 — Facilitator
quote: Through the `/verify` endpoint the facilitator confirms that the client's payment payload meets the server's declared payment requirements; through `/settle` it submits the payment to the blockchain based on the `scheme` and `networkId` of the Payment Payload and waits for the payment to be confirmed on the blockchain.

title: x402 — Exact Scheme
quote: Uses token-native `transferWithAuthorization`, commonly for USDC. This is the default when supported. ... Uses Uniswap Permit2 plus the x402 exact proxy, so it can support ERC-20 tokens without EIP-3009.

title: x402 — Upto Scheme
quote: The buyer signs once for the maximum, and the server chooses a final amount that is less than or equal to that maximum. ... `upto` uses Permit2 because the settled amount is not known when the buyer signs.

title: x402 spec — Exact scheme (EVM), incl. the ERC-7710 Smart Account Option
quote: 3. ERC-7710 | Smart accounts with delegation support. | Smart Account Option (Paid from ERC-7710 compatible account). | One-time use and multi-use. ... This asset transfer method uses ERC-7710 smart contract delegation to authorize transfers from accounts that support the standard. A `DelegationManager` contract implementing the `ERC7710Manager` interface must be deployed on the network. ... The payload field must contain: delegationManager ...; permissionContext ...; delegator .... The process of obtaining a delegation is outside the scope of x402.

title: x402 Payments with Delegations — MetaMask Smart Accounts Kit 1.5.0
quote: With ERC-7710, a buyer's smart account creates a delegation that authorizes the facilitator to transfer tokens on their behalf. The buyer doesn't sign a direct token approval. Instead, they sign a delegation that the facilitator redeems during settlement. ... Buyers can restrict delegations to specific facilitator addresses, amounts, and time windows using delegation scopes. They can also create long lived delegations that allow recurring payments without re-signing for each request.

title: ERC-3009: Transfer With Authorization
quote: A set of functions to enable meta-transactions and atomic interactions with ERC-20 token contracts via signatures conforming to the EIP-712 typed message signing specification.

title: coinbase/x402 — A payments protocol for the internet. Built on HTTP
quote: x402 is an open standard for internet native payments. It aims to support all networks (both crypto & fiat) and forms of value (stablecoins, tokens, fiat).

title: Welcome to x402 — Coinbase Developer Documentation
quote: Payments can be made via EIP-3009 (USDC, EURC) or Permit2 (any ERC-20).
